dedupe_keys.name: weap water evaluation and adaptation planning system stockholm environment institute

description: WEAP is a desktop system from the Stockholm Environment Institute for integrated water resources planning. Users build a schematic of the water system on a GIS map and simulate water demand, supply, runoff, streamflow, storage, pollution generation, treatment and discharge; an embedded linear program solves allocation, built-in hydrology covers rainfall-runoff, evapotranspiration, crop needs and groundwater interaction, and a financial module compares costs and benefits across scenarios. It represents existing and planned infrastructure such as reservoirs, transfers and treatment alongside municipal and agricultural demands. Coverage is any basin or system worldwide; SEI shows uses in California and for strategic water plans in Chile. WEAP runs on Windows; a read-only evaluation version is free after registration, and saving models or using the API needs a paid term licence, priced by user type. Caveats: Windows only (other systems through a virtual machine), single-user, and copying the unlock code is forbidden. Simulation uses: water supply and demand scenarios, allocation and infrastructure planning under climate change. Related records: the CWatM community water model (model-iiasa-cwatm-community-water-model) and CRSS for the Colorado River (model-usbr-crss-crmms-colorado-river).
